# Authentication & session (his-frontend + his-backend GraphQL)

**Goal:** a hospital staff member can sign in to HISv3, keep the session while working, and sign out
again — and the backend never tells an attacker whether an account exists.

**Docs:** test doc [his-frontend-testing.md](../../his-frontend-testing.md) · module features: [module catalogue](../../modules/README.md) (linked on every story).

Source of the stories: cluster `D-HISV3-AUTH` of the QA assessment
(`his-v3-ai/services-impl/202611/backend-rest-e2e-qa-assessment/data-integration/D-HISV3-AUTH/`).
The `D-HISV3-AUTH US-xx` references in every story point back to it.

Surfaces under test:

| Surface                                                      | Target       | Spec folder                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| GraphQL `user` module (`userLogin`, `userLogout`, `userGet`) | his-backend  | `tests/api/graphql/his-backend/user/` |
| Login form, session, logout                                  | his-frontend | `tests/web/his-frontend/auth/`        |

## User stories

- **US-AUTH-01** ([A13.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-03), [A13.02](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-02)) — As a hospital staff member I want to sign in with my User ID and password so that I can work with the menus my access group allows (D-HISV3-AUTH US-01).
- **US-AUTH-02** ([A13.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-03)) — As a signed-in staff member I want my session to survive the next page so that I do not have to sign in again (D-HISV3-AUTH US-02).
- **US-AUTH-03** ([A13.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-03)) — As a staff member who mistypes the password I want a clear message so that I know what to correct (D-HISV3-AUTH US-03).
- **US-AUTH-04** ([A13.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-03)) — As a staff member who finished working I want to sign out so that the next person cannot use my access on a shared computer (D-HISV3-AUTH US-04).
- **US-AUTH-07** ([A13.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-03), [A13.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-01)) — As a supervisor I want to sign in on behalf of a practitioner so that I can complete administration for the patients that practitioner holds (D-HISV3-AUTH US-07).
- **US-AUTH-08** ([A13.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-03)) — As a security officer I want the REST login endpoint to verify the credentials so that no token is issued without a correct password (D-HISV3-AUTH US-08, gap).
- **US-AUTH-10** ([A13.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-03), [A13.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a13-01)) — As a security officer I want the practitioner list to verify the caller identity so that it is not readable without a session (D-HISV3-AUTH US-10, gap).

## Dedicated accounts per role

The role case does not run as the superadmin of the session setup. The dedicated accounts live in
`test-data/private/credentials.<TEST_ENV>.json` — one entry per role (`role`, `username`, `password`).
Without an entry for the role the spec skips itself with a reason; the file is filled per environment
from the password manager, never committed.

## Not covered by this epic

- **REST `POST /api/v1/auth/login`** (D-HISV3-AUTH US-08 / finding AUTH-01). The endpoint still issues a
  token for a hardcoded user without comparing the password. It is not part of the GraphQL or web surface
  of this epic; the row above keeps it visible in the backlog.
- **Forgotten password** (D-HISV3-AUTH US-06, `passwordResetVerifyIdentity` / `passwordResetRequestOtp` /
  `passwordResetConfirm`). It sends an OTP to a mailbox, so it cannot be automated reliably.
- **Impersonated login with a real practitioner** (D-HISV3-AUTH US-07 happy path). The practitioner list is
  guarded by a hardcoded secret (finding AUTH-17); only the form validation is automated here.
- **Login audit** (D-HISV3-AUTH US-05): `log_login_session` is a database table, not an API surface.
